bindings.label: Patient developed left ear pain, hearing loss, purulent and blood-stained discharge, and left facial palsy after ear syringing

A woman in her 70s presented with impacted cerumen in the right ear and underwent two attempts at bilateral irrigation by a practice nurse; immediately after syringing, she reported pain and hearing loss in the left ear and subsequently developed purulent and blood-stained discharge in that ear

ENT examination found severe otitis externa with inflammation of the external auditory canal precluding a view of the tympanic membrane; after removal of a wick, a small anteroinferior perforation of the tympanic membrane was visualized
Patient developed left facial palsy with lagophthalmos, good static tone of the mouth, but weak movement on smiling (House-Brackman V)
CT shows fluid in left middle ear and mastoid without bone erosion
Audiometry confirms mixed hearing loss and tympanic membrane perforation
Traumatic tympanic membrane perforation with secondary otitis media/mastoiditis caused by ear syringing
Tympanometry confirms tympanic membrane perforation and middle ear dysfunction
Facial nerve palsy is due to inflammatory involvement of the facial nerve secondary to otitis media/mastoiditis
